text:
After a 5-2 home loss to Montreal on Thursday, David Pastrnak was the one saying the uncomfortable thing. Audacy's headline had him calling the team's start "unacceptable," and Heavy reported him saying winning had been masking a bigger problem.

His own start is fine. He has 24 points in 19 games (8 goals, 16 assists), and he is shooting 11.9%, right on his usual rate. Daily Faceoff counted him and Pavel Zacha among the league's elite duos.

The flag is around him rather than on him. Boston has scored 5.4 more goals than its chances deserve with Pastrnak on the ice, which is padding the assist total, and at five on five the Bruins are only even in shot attempts when he plays. Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he faced top competition with weaker teammates than most stars, which explains some of that.

Our range still has him finishing between 89 and 119 points, 103 in the middle. What to watch: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 82nd percentile for chances from in front of the net. If Boston's problem is getting there, he is the one who can.
